title: Prototype four different scheduling collision models
summary: Create four comparable direct-manipulation prototypes, then preserve one model while borrowing one preview gesture.
originNote: Distilled from a history-derived practice of prototyping genuinely different interaction physics before selecting and refining one specimen.

setup.instructions: Mount the common scheduling packet. Build all hypotheses in one self-contained comparison artifact; do not import libraries.

turns.content: Read fixtures/schedule.json and build index.html containing four isolated runnable phone-width prototypes for the exact same move. Each prototype must embody a different user model for collision—not merely different styling—and must state in the artifact the one-sentence hypothesis it tests. During pointer movement, make the prospective consequence visible before release; provide undo and a reduced-motion mode. Keep the same activities, times, and 390px viewport across all four. Give each prototype a data-prototype value from 1 through 4.

Now add a fifth final specimen to the same artifact. Use prototype 2 as the interaction model and visual base. Borrow only prototype 4's long-press preview gesture, naming that borrowed behavior in a small provenance note. Preserve prototype 2's collision consequence, geometry, and release semantics. Mark the result data-prototype="final".

checks.description: Four hypotheses and the final synthesis are present.
Run the same move, cancellation, undo, and reduced-motion checks in every specimen and inspect whether consequences truly differ.
